faqs.question: What does the AFB-Smear Examination by Fluorescent Stain – Pus, Abscess, and Aspirates measure?
faqs.answer: The AFB-Smear Examination by Fluorescent Stain – Pus, Abscess, and Aspirates tests for the presence of acid-fast bacilli (AFB) which are specific to the Mycobacterium tuberculosis bacterium in pus, abscess, and aspirate samples.

faqs.question: Why is the AFB-Smear Examination by Fluorescent Stain – Pus, Abscess, and Aspirates done?
faqs.answer: • To diagnose active tuberculosis infection • To monitor the effectiveness of TB treatment • To identify other mycobacterial infections • To assess the risk of spreading tuberculosis to others

faqs.question: When is the AFB-Smear Examination by Fluorescent Stain – Pus, Abscess, and Aspirates recommended and who should take the test?
faqs.answer: Your doctor may recommend this test if you have • Symptoms suggestive of tuberculosis such as persistent cough, fever, weight loss, and night sweats. • Pus or abscess formation in a site with suspected tuberculosis infection. • A history of contact with someone diagnosed with active tuberculosis. • A weakened immune system or other risk factors for tuberculosis.

faqs.question: What if the results of the AFB-Smear Examination by Fluorescent Stain – Pus, Abscess, and Aspirates are abnormal?
faqs.answer: Abnormal results may indicate a possible tuberculosis infection or other mycobacterial infections.

faqs.question: What to expect during the AFB-Smear Examination by Fluorescent Stain – Pus, Abscess, and Aspirates?
faqs.answer: • A small sample of pus, abscess fluid, or aspirate will be collected from the affected area. • The sample will be sent to the laboratory for microscopic examination using a fluorescent stain. • The test is painless and only takes a few minutes to perform.

faqs.question: What preparations are required before the AFB-Smear Examination by Fluorescent Stain – Pus, Abscess, and Aspirates?
faqs.answer: To prepare for this test: • Inform your doctor about any medications you are taking as they might interfere with the test results. • No specific dietary or lifestyle restrictions are necessary before this test. Please reach out to your healthcare provider for any specific requirements.

faqs.question: What other tests may be ordered with the AFB-Smear Examination by Fluorescent Stain – Pus, Abscess, and Aspirates?
faqs.answer: • GeneXpert MTB/RIF assay: This test detects the DNA of Mycobacterium tuberculosis (TB) and resistance to rifampicin, an important TB drug. • Chest X-ray: This imaging test helps visualize lung abnormalities associated with tuberculosis.

faqs.question: What is the AFB-Smear Examination by Fluorescent Stain – Pus, Abscess, and Aspirates also known as?
faqs.answer: Acid-fast bacilli (AFB) smear test, Fluorescent stain for AFB, AFB microscopy

faqs.question: What is tuberculosis (TB)?
faqs.answer: Tuberculosis (TB) is a contagious bacterial infection caused by Mycobacterium tuberculosis. It primarily affects the lungs but can also spread to other parts of the body, such as the brain, spine, and kidneys. TB is transmitted through droplets when an infected person coughs or sneezes.
